metrics.name: Class imbalance ratio
metrics.definition: Images in the largest class divided by images in the smallest class.
metrics.interpretation: The largest class has 4,379 images and the smallest 149, a 29.4x spread.
metrics.recommendation: Use class-weighted loss or a balanced sampler, and report per-class metrics rather than accuracy.

metrics.name: Gini coefficient
metrics.definition: Inequality of the class-size distribution, 0 perfectly even and 1 maximally skewed.
metrics.interpretation: Class sizes have a Gini coefficient of 0.371.
metrics.recommendation: Distribution inequality is moderate.

metrics.name: Distribution evenness
metrics.definition: Shannon entropy of class sizes normalised to [0, 1]; 1 means all classes are equal.
metrics.interpretation: Evenness is 0.934 across 38 classes.
metrics.recommendation: Evenness below 0.6 usually needs resampling before benchmark use.

metrics.name: Rare classes
metrics.definition: Classes holding fewer than 25% of the mean class size.
metrics.interpretation: 3 of 38 classes are rare.
metrics.recommendation: Collect more images for these classes or merge them into a coarser label.

metrics.name: Undersized classes
metrics.definition: Classes with fewer than the configured minimum of 20 images.
metrics.interpretation: Every class meets the configured minimum size.
metrics.recommendation: No action needed.

metrics.name: Long-tail concentration
metrics.definition: Number of classes needed to cover 80% of all images, and the share left to the tail.
metrics.method: Cumulative share over classes sorted by size
metrics.interpretation: 22 of 38 classes cover 80% of images; the remaining tail holds 19.3%.
metrics.recommendation: Report tail-class performance separately; aggregate accuracy hides it.

metrics.name: Split feasibility
metrics.definition: Classes too small to place at least one image in each split at ratios 0.70/0.15/0.15.
metrics.interpretation: Every class can be split at the configured ratios.
metrics.recommendation: No action needed.

metrics.name: Visual diversity
metrics.definition: Mean pairwise perceptual-hash distance, normalised by hash length.
metrics.method: mean Hamming distance over 199,915 sampled pairs / 64 bits
metrics.interpretation: Images differ by 30.0 of 64 hash bits on average (46.9% normalised).
metrics.recommendation: Diversity is healthy for a benchmark corpus.

metrics.name: Unique perceptual hashes
metrics.definition: Share of images with a perceptual hash no other image shares exactly.
metrics.interpretation: 100.00% of images have a distinct perceptual hash.
metrics.recommendation: No action needed.

metrics.name: Duplicate ratio
metrics.definition: Share of images flagged as exact duplicates by the quality gate.
metrics.interpretation: 0.00% of images are exact duplicates of another image.
metrics.recommendation: No action needed.

metrics.name: Near-duplicate ratio
metrics.definition: Share of images flagged as perceptually near-identical to a retained image.
metrics.interpretation: 0.00% of images are near duplicates.
metrics.recommendation: No action needed.

metrics.name: Least diverse classes
metrics.definition: Classes whose members are most visually similar to each other.
metrics.method: Normalised mean pairwise hash distance within each class
metrics.interpretation: Lowest-diversity class: raspberry___healthy (0.39), grape___black_rot (0.40), grape___healthy (0.40), grape___esca_black_measles (0.40), potato___healthy (0.41)
metrics.recommendation: Classes below 0.15 are often a single photo session; treat their scores with caution.

metrics.name: Source diversity
metrics.definition: Entropy of the per-source image counts, normalised to [0, 1].
metrics.interpretation: 1 source(s) contribute: color 100.0%
metrics.recommendation: A single-source corpus cannot support cross-source generalisation claims.

metrics.name: Source-dominated classes
metrics.definition: Classes where one source supplies more than 80% of the images.
metrics.interpretation: 38 classes are dominated by a single source.
metrics.recommendation: A model can learn the source's capture conditions instead of the disease; evaluate cross-source held-out performance.

metrics.name: Single-source classes
metrics.definition: Classes whose images all come from one contributing dataset.
metrics.interpretation: 38 of 38 classes come from one source.
metrics.recommendation: Expected when datasets cover different crops; a concern when they overlap.

metrics.name: Label consistency
metrics.definition: Share of raw folder labels that map to exactly one canonical label.
metrics.interpretation: Every raw label resolves to exactly one canonical label.
metrics.recommendation: No action needed.

metrics.name: Resolution consistency across sources
metrics.definition: Relative spread of mean megapixels between sources.
metrics.method: (max - min) / max of per-source mean megapixels
metrics.interpretation: Mean megapixels per source: color 0.07
metrics.recommendation: Large gaps let a model identify the source from image size alone; resizing at packaging time removes the shortcut.

metrics.name: Quality consistency across sources
metrics.definition: Relative spread of mean quality score between sources.
metrics.method: (max - min) / max of per-source mean quality score
metrics.interpretation: Mean quality per source: color 0.764
metrics.recommendation: Systematic quality gaps between sources bias any cross-source comparison.

metrics.name: Duplicate clusters
metrics.definition: Groups of images identified as identical or perceptually near-identical.
metrics.method: Clusters produced by the quality stage's duplicate detector
metrics.interpretation: 522 clusters cover 1,772 images; the largest holds 223.
metrics.recommendation: Clusters are the unit that must stay inside one split.

metrics.name: Images at risk of leaking
metrics.definition: Images in clusters that still hold more than one retained image after the quality gate.
metrics.method: sum(retained members) over clusters with more than one retained member
metrics.interpretation: The quality gate already retained at most one image per cluster; nothing can leak.
metrics.recommendation: No action needed.

metrics.name: Naive-split leak probability
metrics.definition: Chance an at-risk cluster would straddle two partitions under an ungrouped split.
metrics.method: mean over clusters of 1 - sum(ratio ^ retained members)
metrics.interpretation: No cluster can straddle a split.
metrics.recommendation: Grouped splitting reduces this to zero by construction.

metrics.name: Cross-class duplicate clusters
metrics.definition: Clusters whose members carry more than one canonical label.
metrics.interpretation: 151 clusters contain images labelled differently.
metrics.recommendation: These are either annotation conflicts or perceptual-hash false positives. Review analytics/leakage_report.csv, then either fix the labels or tighten quality.duplicates.max_hamming_distance / set across_classes to false.

metrics.name: Cross-dataset overlap
metrics.definition: Clusters whose members come from more than one contributing dataset.
metrics.interpretation: No image appears in more than one source.
metrics.recommendation: Overlap inflates the apparent size of a merged corpus; report the deduplicated count.
